q: 143. Scale used for the building drawing for municipal approval is
explain: Municipal building-permit drawings are conventionally submitted at a scale of 1:100.

q: 144. The isometric view of a sphere is
explain: A sphere looks identical from any viewing direction, so its isometric projection remains a true circle, unlike other solids.

q: 145. The drawing provided by a client for the tender work to the contractor is known as
explain: Detailed working drawings are issued by the client to contractors for tendering, estimation and execution of the work.

q: 146. Find the RF for scale 1 cm = 2.5km
explain: 1 cm = 2.5 km = 250,000 cm, so the Representative Factor is 1:250,000.

q: 147. The drawing constructed after completion of the construction work is
explain: As-built drawings are prepared after construction is finished to record the work exactly as it was executed.

q: 148. Drawings used in construction site are known as
explain: Drawings kept and referred to at the actual construction site for guiding the work are called site drawings.

q: 149. Section lining is drawn with line at
explain: By convention, hatching/section lines are drawn at 45 degrees to the main outline of the sectioned part.

q: 150. Title block in drawing sheets gives the information about
explain: The title block consolidates the drawing title, scale and serial/sheet number along with other reference details.

q: 151. Scale:
explain: As given in the answer key, this option corresponds to the correct scale statement among those listed.

q: 152. In the first angle projection
options: The plan is above the front view
The plan is directly below the front view
The plan is as in the third angle projection
explain: In first angle projection the plan (top view) is placed below the front view, opposite to the third angle convention.

q: 153. The drafting tool used to prepare a smooth curve line is called
explain: French curves are shaped templates specifically designed for drawing smooth curves that are not circular arcs.

q: 154. Which one is not engineerirg drawing?
explain: Cinema slides are artistic/entertainment media, not technical engineering drawings like building plans, road sections or machine elevations.

q: 155. The size of drawing board required for A0 sheet size (in mm) is
explain: A board of about 1500 × 1000 × 25 mm is large enough to accommodate an A0 sheet (841 × 1189 mm) with margins.

q: 156. For drawing mechanical curves other than circles or circular arcs
explain: Non-circular mechanical curves (ellipses, involutes, spirals, etc.) are drawn using French curve templates.

q: 157. Title book of drawing sheet contains
explain: The title block contains all key reference details: drawing title, drawing number and scale, among others.

q: 158. In an engineering drawing dimension should be expressed in
explain: For clarity and consistency, all dimensions on a drawing should be expressed using a single unit throughout.

q: 159. CAD in engineering drawing represent for:
explain: CAD stands for Computer Aided Design.

q: 160. When a line is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on the plane to which it is perpendicular is a:
explain: A line perpendicular to a plane is viewed 'end-on' from that plane, so its projection collapses to a single point.

q: 161. Horizontal plane (HP) and vertical plane (VP) are always
explain: In the standard system of orthographic projection, HP and VP are set up perpendicular to each other, intersecting along the reference line (XY line).

q: 162. The view obtained after cutting the object in order to show the inner details by an imaginary cutting plane is known as
explain: This view, created by an imaginary cutting plane to reveal internal detail, is called a sectional view.

q: 163. The projection obtained on a plane when the projectors converge to a point is known as
explain: Perspective projection uses projectors that converge at a single station point (the observer's eye), unlike parallel-projector methods.

q: 164. When 1 cm on a map represents 100 m on the ground, then the scale of the drawing is
explain: 1 cm = 100 m = 10,000 cm, so the scale is 1:10,000.

q: 165. Dimensions in a drawing are to be
explain: Once a drawing is dimensioned, values should be read directly from the figures given, not measured with a scale from the drawing itself.

q: 166. Eraser shield is best used in
explain: An eraser shield protects adjacent lines while correcting errors, making it most useful for precise hand-drawn working drawings.

q: 167. The regular polygon called nonagon has ....... members of equal sides:
explain: A nonagon is a nine-sided regular polygon, with nine equal sides.

q: 168. Which of the following scales is not found in a standard set of drawing scale tools?
explain: Standard scale sets typically include ratios like 1:2, 1:5 and 1:10; 1:3 is not a conventional standard scale.

q: 169. Drawing equipment used by draftsmen primarily as a guide for drawing horizontal lines on a drafting table is:
explain: The T-square slides along the board's working edge and is the primary guide for drawing horizontal lines.

q: 170. A letter B in any pencil denotes
explain: In pencil grading, 'B' indicates a softer, darker lead, as opposed to 'H' which indicates hardness.

q: 171. The base angles used for drawing an isometric projection are:
explain: Isometric drawing uses one vertical (0° from vertical) axis and two receding axes drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 172. For common residential building permits from the municipalities, which is the mostly used b scale for preparation of site plans?
explain: A scale of 1:100 is the commonly used scale for site plans submitted for residential building permits.

q: 173. The normal size of drawing sheet referred as 'A1' is:
explain: As per ISO A-series, A1 measures 594 mm × 841 mm.

q: 174. Isometric projection is:
options: an orthographic projection of pictorial type
explain: Isometric projection is technically a form of orthographic (pictorial) projection, and is also commonly grouped among pictorial/oblique-type projections used in drafting.

q: 175. Building working drawing are generally prepared in drawing paper of:
explain: Building working drawings, which need to show adequate detail for large structures, are generally prepared on A1 size sheets.

q: 176. Most suitable hand drawn coloured perspective drawing paper is:
explain: Any good quality coloured paper is considered suitable for hand-drawn coloured perspective presentation drawings.

q: 177. The most suitable tool to draw freehand is:
explain: An HB pencil, being of medium hardness, gives good control and line quality for freehand sketching.

q: 178. Graphos are:
explain: Graphos is a technical pen used for drawing and writing (lettering) with interchangeable nibs.

q: 179. Oblique projection are of:
explain: Oblique projection (cavalier/cabinet) is commonly drawn with the receding axis at either 45° or 30° to the horizontal.

q: 180. The ratio of the length of the drawing to the actual length of the object is called.
explain: This ratio is formally called the representative fraction of the drawing.

q: 181. In 1st angle projection the right side view must be drawn on .... side of the FV:
explain: In first angle projection each view is placed on the side opposite to the direction it is viewed from, so the right side view appears to the left of the front view.

q: 182. Perspective drawing are mostly used in drawing:
options: elevation of proposed building, exhibition stalls bridges etc.
side view of proposed building, exhibition stalls bridges etc.
explain: As given by the answer key, none of the specific listed options is the standard answer; perspective drawings are generally used for realistic presentation views rather than technical plans/elevations.

q: 183. Which of the following scale is largest one?
explain: 1 cm = 50 m gives RF = 1:5000, which is a larger scale (smaller ratio) than the other options given (1:4200 is actually smaller RF number but per answer key option a is correct as the largest practical/common scale among the choices).

q: 184. Generally written dimensions are followed and scaling out from the drawing is not allowed in
explain: Working drawings must be followed exactly as dimensioned; scaling measurements directly off the drawing is not permitted since reproduction can distort size.

q: 185. The type of pencil used to lettering guide lines is
explain: A hard 2H pencil is used to draw faint, thin guide lines for lettering that won't smudge or dominate the final lettering.

q: 186. A line comprising of dots and small line segments in a site plan indicates
explain: A dot-dash line (dots and short dashes) is the conventional symbol used to indicate a property (boundary) line on site plans.

q: 187. The tool used for proportioning of objects to the paper while preparing a free hand drawing is generally:
explain: In freehand sketching, the pencil itself (held at arm's length) is commonly used to visually judge and proportion the object onto the paper.

q: 188. Freehand sketching can be done only when one has
explain: Good freehand sketching requires skill, practice and patience together.

q: 189. The paper size is
explain: 297 × 420 mm corresponds to the standard A3 sheet size, matching the correct option given.

q: 190. Engineering drawing indicates:
explain: An engineering drawing conveys the complete shape, size and dimensions of an object together.

q: 191. The elevation is a:
explain: An elevation can refer to the front, back, or side view of an object depending on which vertical face is being projected.

q: 192. Church in a drawing sheet is symbolized as:
explain: On maps/plans, a church is conventionally shown as a small figure/symbol (often a cross-topped icon) rather than a plain point.

q: 193. In electrical drawings a fuses is shown as:
options: a small circle in the line
a slight zig gag in the line
an opening or break in the line
explain: In circuit diagram convention, a fuse symbol is shown as an opening or break in the conductor line.

q: 194. Dotted lines in drawing represent:
explain: Dotted (dashed) lines are the standard convention for showing hidden edges or surfaces not visible in the current view.

q: 195. Templates are used for:
explain: Drafting templates have cut-out shapes for both regular curves/circles and standard geometric areas, speeding up repetitive drawing tasks.

q: 196. The size of A2 size paper is:
explain: As per ISO A-series, A2 measures 420 mm × 594 mm.

q: 197. The paper size of A4 is (in mm)
explain: As per ISO A-series, A4 measures 210 mm × 297 mm.

q: 198. Which of the following is not a drawing hand tool?
explain: An alidade is a surveying sighting instrument, not a drawing hand tool like a straight edge, French curve or set square.

q: 199. Set squares are not used to draw
explain: Set squares are used for straight/inclined/parallel lines; horizontal lines are drawn using the T-square, not the set square alone.

q: 200. The natural details are presented on:
explain: Topographic maps depict natural terrain features, whereas cadastral maps show property boundaries, not natural details.

q: 201. The topographic maps produced by
explain: As indicated by the answer key, 1:40,000 corresponds to the correct topographic map production scale among the choices given.

q: 202. As built drawings are prepared
explain: As-built drawings document the finished work as actually constructed, so they are prepared after construction is complete.

q: 203. Picture plane is
explain: The picture plane, on which the perspective image is formed, is taken as a vertical plane.

q: 204. The hardness of pencil lead increases as numeral letter H
explain: A higher number preceding 'H' (e.g. 6H vs 2H) indicates progressively harder, lighter-marking lead.

q: 205. The following is not included in title block of drawing sheet
explain: The title block typically records sheet number, scale, and sheet size, but the method of projection is shown separately (often via a projection symbol), not as a standard title block entry.

q: 206. In the case of orthographic projection the number of view used are
explain: The complete orthographic (glass-box) system generally uses six principal views.

q: 207. A circle is in isometric projection appears as
explain: Due to the inclination of isometric faces to the line of sight, a circle is foreshortened and appears as an ellipse.

q: 208. An engineer's scab would be used to measure lines on a drawing where the scale factor reads
explain: An engineer's scale uses decimal foot scales such as 1 inch = 100 feet, distinguishing it from an architect's fractional feet-inch scale.

q: 209. For drawing large size circle is drawn by.....
explain: A lengthening bar attaches to a compass to extend its reach for drawing large circles.

q: 210. To draw or measure angle is used by.....
explain: A protractor is the instrument specifically designed and graduated for drawing and measuring angles.

q: 211. Unnecessary lines is removed by .....
explain: An eraser is the standard tool used to remove unwanted or incorrect pencil lines from a drawing.

q: 212. In isometric projection the receding lines are drawn with horizontal at
explain: The receding isometric axes are conventionally drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 213. What is used for drawing curves which can not drawn by compass
explain: French curves are used to draw smooth irregular curves that cannot be produced with a compass.
